attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his reply to Booch on his Substack. They come under 'In my darkest moments', but he does assert as fact that the money is mostly going to LLMs.

semantics.note: The checkable core is that most of the money is going to LLMs. Reading 'not' as a typo is reasonable. 'AI money' widens the scope: the paragraph before refers to money 'somewhat directed at the problem' of AGI. The opinion parts stay opinion.

contract.note: The contract counts all AI money, including internal corporate and public research spending, and picks Q4 2022 itself. In context Marcus means money aimed at general intelligence, so this broad denominator stretches his loose wording against him. The result depends on that choice.

evidence.note: CB Insights: 2022 annual AI venture funding of $45.8B, with Q4 at $9.3B. It has no LLM breakdown and leaves out internal and public spending, so it does not measure the claimed share.

OECD, citing CB Insights: about $2.6B of generative AI private funding in 2022. That is annual, generative AI rather than LLMs, and venture money only. It does not match the contract's denominator or period.

reviews.rationale: Neither item measures the LLM share of the money in question for the target period. The venture figures (2.6B against 45.8B) hint at a small share, but generative AI is not the same as LLMs, the figures are annual, and they cover a different denominator. The contract's broad denominator is also unfair to Marcus's contextual meaning. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own closing line in his exchange with Booch.

semantics.note: 'Architecture is all' is an emphatic slogan about how much integration matters. Calling it 'the decisive problem' picks a comparative reading the speaker did not spell out. It is rhetoric, not an observation that can be checked.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no non-arbitrary support or contradiction test and rightly declines to read 'all' literally or as a ranking.

reviews.rationale: This is an emphatic statement of priority with no defined boundary for 'architecture' and no way to measure it. No empirical test can fairly score it, so it is not adjudicable.
